crime: She was the prison's first-responder. When anything went wrong, hands reached for her.
A fire had once taken the unprepared on a clear, ordinary afternoon. She drilled for everything after.
One girl mocked her drilling in front of everyone — nothing goes wrong on a calm day — and mocked it again that evening at the showers.
In the shower that girl slipped and struck her head on the stone. The drain had clogged; water pooled, and she lay face-down in it. The others called, and she came.
She went to work on the girl. She held the airway shut, deliberately, through the one moment it needed to be open.
The girl did not come back. What remained was a body dead of a fall and water, and a responder who, by all appearances, had done everything.
A girl had knelt beside her through the work — one who had learned the reviving procedure from watching her. That girl caught the single step held wrong, at the moment it had to be right.
Every case before had been flawless. The single deviation came at the single one she had reason to lose.
fields.epitaph: She drilled for every disaster but the one her drilling made.
fields.epithet: She Who Had Drilled for Everything
execution: On the execution stand, a heavy iron vessel of burning oil hung above her from a single cord. The cord rose from the vessel through the jaws of a shear fixed at her hand, then up to an overhead anchor.
A flame was lit at the top of the cord and began burning through, working its way down toward the vessel.
Her hands closed the shear on the cord below the flame — the textbook break in a fire-line.
The cord was all that held the vessel. The burning oil came down on her.

magic.name: the Drill
magic.text: The Drill — In a genuine emergency, her body performs the trained response she never trained: the right knot, the compression rhythm, the fire-line order.
